The first body block is the H1 heading with the episode title linked to the episode when a URL is known: - # [Episode Title](https://example.com/episode). Without a URL, use a plain - # Episode Title.

A producer-owned session opens with an optional short description, artwork when available, and a directly playable MP3 recording. The recording’s Logseq/Entity/Asset page holds its file metadata. Artwork and audio use Markdown media embeds with the asset URLs: ![Episode artwork](https://example.com/artwork.gif) and ![Episode recording](https://example.com/recording.mp3).

Downloadable MicroFreak patches use labeled Markdown links to the files, such as [Download MicroFreak preset A](https://example.com/preset-A.mfpz), so listeners can download them from the episode page. An episode published as a YouTube video is also a Logseq/Entity/YouTube instance, Episode first: logseq-entity:: [[Logseq/Entity/Podcast/Episode]], [[Logseq/Entity/YouTube]]. The page keeps the episode path under its show. The YouTube video ID becomes a deduplication key alongside the episode URL.
Sources — a ## Sources section links the episode page, the YouTube recording, and the episode when one exists.

Timestamps — every timestamp is a video time in seconds, written {{youtube-timestamp <seconds>}}. Times from an audio app such as Snipd are converted to video time. The audio and video versions can differ by an intro or an ad break, so check each converted time against the transcript line it should land on.
Chapters — a ## Video section holds the {{video <watch URL>}} block. Each YouTube chapter is an H3 beneath it: ### {{youtube-timestamp <seconds>}} <Chapter Title>.

Snips — a Snipd snip is an H4 under the chapter that contains it, with a Snipd: URL line, a short summary, and a Transcript child set to collapsed:: true. The transcript groups lines under a speaker's person page, each line starting with its own timestamp.

Highlights — a Readwise highlight made while watching is a bare {{youtube-timestamp <seconds>}} block placed in time order next to the snips. Speaker children hold the quoted text as > quotes, ending with a link back to the highlight in Readwise.
Expansion — chapters that hold the author's highlights stay expanded. Chapters without highlights are collapsed:: true.

What only the video shows — slides, diagrams, code, and screens that the audio does not describe are captured as frames. A frame is saved in assets/, named from the page path with the video second and a short caption, and embedded under the timestamp block where it appears. A child bullet under the image transcribes its text or describes the diagram, so the page reads in full without the video.

In this garden, Synth Preset pages model saved synthesizer sounds and the evidence needed to describe or restore them.

A saved sound includes the settings and sequences stored by its instrument. A device slot is its current location. Stable page titles preserve links from composition and performance logs when metadata changes.

The name appears once in the filename and once in its instrument-specific name property. The body starts with - # Notes and holds listening observations, performance notes and links to music logs. Empty notes remain a heading without generated descriptions.

Sync owns documented device metadata in frontmatter and preserves handwritten body content. Sound descriptions require listening or verified parameters; a category and name cannot establish a signal chain.
An instance’s logseq-entity:: links to its data definition, using the narrowest known type such as Logseq/Entity/Preset/Synth/Microfreak. Shared properties follow Logseq/Frontmatter.

Keys start with the owning type’s lowercase, hyphen-separated path: Preset/Synth gives preset-synth-; Preset/Synth/Microfreak gives preset-synth-microfreak-. Each property is documented under its owner’s Frontmatter/<literal-key> page as a Logseq/Entity/Frontmatter/Definition.

Each property definition has the literal key as an alias, connecting the clickable property name to its namespaced dictionary. Logseq Properties describes property pages; Logseq aliases describes alias references. Existing standalone pages with the same key need reconciliation before adding an alias.

Categorical values are explicit links to the definition’s child value pages; numeric and Boolean values retain their scalar types. A linked instrument model can supply an existing categorical vocabulary.
Numbered collections use and for adjacent populated slots. A page absent from the device has neither navigation property.

Human-readable properties describe verified parameters. Exact exports preserve data that may still lack a decoded dictionary. A complete reconstruction also needs referenced samples or wavetables, applicable global settings and the firmware context.

New parameter definitions state the source encoding, units, range, enum values and conversion, including raw values when a display conversion loses precision. Unknown parameters remain absent. A file digest identifies the exported bytes; it does not establish that every parameter has been decoded.
A Markdown link or URL to an exported preset file whose destination has been checked. Omit while no export is available.
The file preserves the format produced by its exporter. Restoration confidence requires the matching instrument, firmware and any separately stored sample or wavetable dependencies.
The 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters of SHA-256 computed over the exact bytes linked by Logseq/Entity/Preset/Synth/Frontmatter/preset-synth-file. Omit until the file exists.
A digest detects changes to that file. Equivalent sounds can have different export bytes, so a digest does not prove musical equivalence.
The established provenance of a saved sound. A slot number or name alone cannot establish provenance.
A sound established as user-created or modified from another sound.
A sound verified against an identified factory release or export.
The sound’s provenance has not been established.
In this garden, MicroFreak Synth Preset pages model individual saved sounds on the Microfreak, following Logseq/Entity/Preset/Synth.

Pages use Microfreak/Preset/<slot> <name>, with a three-digit slot and the name observed at creation. The filename remains stable so existing music-log links resolve. A newly observed name at an occupied slot needs a new page when continuity is unknown.

Microfreak/Preset/396 Anit and Microfreak/Preset/397 Imit illustrate the frontmatter and notes format. Repeated names or slot numbers alone cannot establish that two observations are the same saved sound.
Shared provenance and export properties are defined by Logseq/Entity/Preset/Synth. Unknown origin uses Logseq/Entity/Preset/Synth/Frontmatter/preset-synth-origin/Unknown.

The saved-header inventory reads slot, name, category and initialization status. It cannot detect a same-name edit to oscillator, filter, envelope, modulation or sequence settings. The Elektroid header decoder supplies the protocol evidence.

Elektroid’s preset download and serialization retain the preset payload for export: up to 146 blocks of 32 bytes. Supported payloads contain labeled raw parameter records for oscillator, filter, envelopes, LFO, modulation routes and preset settings. Repeated live reads matched the corresponding MIDI Control Center export byte for byte; the parameter inspection documentation records the framing and remaining interpretation limits.

The parameter inspection task reads a saved export with mise run microfreak:inspect /private/path/preset.bin or a computer project with mise run microfreak:inspect /private/path/project.mfprojz --slot 1. It reports exact stored bytes and named raw fields, identifies unsupported layouts, and leaves the input unchanged. Its preserves the distinction between raw values and unverified display conversions.

--interpret-fw5 adds the existing firmware 5 interpretations beside the raw fields: supported oscillator model and control names, normalized or metadata-scaled value domains, and source evidence for each interpretation. The report states the firmware assumption; an export does not establish its firmware version. Unknown models retain generic field names, and unsupported values retain their raw readings. The option leaves the raw report and preset notes intact.

Raw values describe saved base settings; modulation, performance gestures and unsaved edits affect the audible sound. Instrument display units, sequence contents, matrix destination meanings and referenced sample or wavetable identities require further verification. Firmware 5 oscillator indices follow the research cited in the optional interpretation report. A computer project can differ from the current device inventory.

Microfreak/UG/17 Ext Gear/09 MIDI CC Control and Microfreak/UG/21 Appendix D - CC Values describe MIDI control changes. A stream of knob movements is incomplete evidence of a saved sound: parameters that never change remain unobserved. Microfreak/UG/04 Presets/05 Digital Control explains why panel positions may differ from recalled values.

Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/03 Types defines oscillator models. Microfreak/UG/04 Presets/03 Preset Config defines per-preset settings, including voice behavior, scale and sequencer options. These guides describe meanings and ranges; values for a particular saved sound need a read or observation of that sound.

Samples and user wavetables have separate export workflows in Microfreak/UG/14 Config/02 MIDI Control Center/03 Samples Tab/01 Management and Microfreak/UG/14 Config/02 MIDI Control Center/02 Wavetables Tab/01 Management. A preset export alone does not establish that those resources are preserved. Global settings such as tuning and tempo behavior also affect playback; see Microfreak/UG/14 Config/02 MIDI Control Center/01 Device Tab.

A saved preset referenced by a published session has notes covering Saved export and provenance, Oscillator, Filter, Envelopes, LFO, Modulation matrix, and Performance and session context. These sections explain supported settings and their control meanings, with cited sources and explicit uncertainty.

Provenance identifies the export, capture date, bank or slot when relevant, and file digest. A verified match to an archived factory payload establishes that saved baseline; it does not establish a session-time capture or the instrument's unsaved state.

Values carry verified units or a clearly named normalized or raw domain. Unknown display conversions, matrix destinations, firmware assumptions and resource identities remain qualified. Large raw inventories stay outside the notes unless their numbers help explain the sound.

Performance notes distinguish what the saved patch supports from changes heard or recorded during a session. An unidentified initialized sound is described plainly rather than assigned an invented numbered preset or presumed settings.
The MicroFreak sync task previews the connected device with mise run microfreak:sync; --apply updates its saved metadata. The sync implementation on GitHub is also available as a .

--save-inventory /tmp/microfreak-inventory.json stores a full inventory; --inventory /tmp/microfreak-inventory.json previews that capture. --garden /absolute/path/to/worktree selects the destination and --port 'Arturia MicroFreak' selects an exact endpoint.

A complete successful inventory updates reported fields, omits initialized slots and marks missing sounds absent. Partial reads write nothing. Handwritten notes, established origin, verified oscillator type and export references survive metadata refreshes. A saved inventory describes its capture time; a new device read is needed to establish current state.
Header sync performs no binary export. File and digest properties are populated only after an export and its destination have been verified.
The category reported in the saved preset header, represented by one of the value pages below. The category labels the sound for browsing; the oscillator engine has its own property.
Elektroid’s category decoder maps the raw category byte to these names. Unknown codes must be reported before importing; their meaning cannot be inferred.

Page-link autocomplete under Logseq/Entity/Preset/Synth/Microfreak/Frontmatter/preset-synth-microfreak-category/ lists the category pages. Logseq Properties explains property names, value autocomplete and page references.
Boolean true or false: the initialization bit in the last saved header. Initialized slots are omitted from the populated preset inventory.
The decoded bit is header[3] & 0x08; see Elektroid preset download.
The saved name returned by the device header, preserved as text. The current importer accepts 1–14 ASCII characters from its documented filename-safe alphabet and rejects unsupported names.
This property is the single occurrence of the preset name in page content. The filename carries the name used when the page was first created.
Integer from 1 to 512: the last observed device slot. A moved sound can retain its page title while this value changes.
The slot locates a saved sound; a slot alone cannot establish the identity of its contents.
Boolean true or false: whether this saved preset matched a populated slot in the latest successful full inventory.
A failed or partial inventory cannot establish absence. false retains the historical page and its notes; adjacent-slot navigation is removed.
A verified oscillator model page under Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/03 Types. The linked guide section defines the engine and the meanings of its Wave, Timbre and Shape controls.
This field is omitted until a saved value has been verified. The saved-header inventory supplies no oscillator type; a category such as Keys cannot determine the engine.
A manual observation must identify the saved preset being observed. The sync preserves this field but a change to other sound parameters requires a fresh verification.

The 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters of SHA-256 over the exact 4672-byte saved parameter payload. The 35-byte device header is excluded. This digest identifies the bytes from which the raw parameter properties were read; it does not establish that every parameter or external resource has been interpreted.
MicroFreak parameter inspector defines the payload boundary and digest. A fresh read with a different digest requires fresh verification of the raw properties.

A saved VCF.Cutoff field as 0x followed by six lowercase hexadecimal digits. The first byte is a raw descriptor; the next two bytes are the raw value in little-endian order. Preserve all three bytes together. The descriptor's meaning, display conversion, units and range are unverified.

MicroFreak parameter inspector documents the serialized field and byte layout. The saved payload is identified by Logseq/Entity/Preset/Synth/Microfreak/Frontmatter/preset-synth-microfreak-parameter-payload-sha256.
Microfreak/UG/07 Filter/01 Modifying Sound/04 Cutoff Frequency names the related human control Cutoff; the guide does not define this saved byte encoding.

A saved VCF.Reso field as 0x followed by six lowercase hexadecimal digits. The first byte is a raw descriptor; the next two bytes are the raw value in little-endian order. Preserve all three bytes together. The descriptor's meaning, display conversion, units and range are unverified.

MicroFreak parameter inspector documents the serialized field and byte layout. The saved payload is identified by Logseq/Entity/Preset/Synth/Microfreak/Frontmatter/preset-synth-microfreak-parameter-payload-sha256.
Microfreak/UG/07 Filter/01 Modifying Sound/05 Resonance names the related human control Resonance; the guide does not define this saved byte encoding.

A saved VCO.Type field as 0x followed by six lowercase hexadecimal digits. The first byte is a raw descriptor; the next two bytes are the raw value in little-endian order. Preserve all three bytes together. The descriptor's meaning, display conversion, units and range are unverified.

MicroFreak parameter inspector documents the serialized field and byte layout. The saved payload is identified by Logseq/Entity/Preset/Synth/Microfreak/Frontmatter/preset-synth-microfreak-parameter-payload-sha256.
Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/02 Param Controls names the related human control Type; the guide does not define this saved byte encoding.
